environment: Humpback whale numbers hit their spring peak off the Queensland coast
Rooftop solar sets a new generation record as spring sunshine kicks in
science: Reef scientists trial a biodegradable shield to help coral beat the heat
sports: Queensland sides gear up as NRL and AFL finals footy begins
stories.overview: A total lunar eclipse will turn the moon blood red over Australia this weekend

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, glad you could join us this Friday. We've got whales cruising past the coast, footy finals kicking off and a blood moon on the way this weekend, so there's plenty to get through. I'm Jamie, and honestly today's one of my favourite line ups in a while. We've got good news for the reef, good news for your power bill, and good news if you love a finals atmosphere. Grab a cuppa and settle in, because we're kicking things off with the environment, and there is a very large marine mammal situation happening just off our beaches right now.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: So Alex, it is peak humpback whale season along the Queensland coast, which means spots like the Gold Coast and Hervey Bay are absolutely buzzing with sightings. Mums and calves are making their way south and whale watchers are reporting bumper numbers this year. Love that, it's basically our own version of a spring migration parade, minus the marching band. Meanwhile on the power front, all that spring sunshine has pushed rooftop solar generation to a fresh record, which is good news for anyone who likes watching their electricity meter run backwards. It really is a nice little one two punch, wildlife thriving and households saving. Two very different kinds of solar powered energy if you think about it, one's got a blowhole and the other's on your roof.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, science time, and this one's close to home for us Queenslanders. Reef researchers have been trialling a biodegradable film, a bit like a sunscreen for coral, that helps shield reefs from heat stress during marine heatwaves. So basically we're giving the Great Barrier Reef its own version of sunnies and a hat. Early trials are promising, and it's a nice reminder that some of the smartest climate solutions are coming right out of our own backyard labs. Exactly, it's not a silver bullet but every bit of breathing room helps while the bigger emissions work happens. Small science, potentially big difference for something as massive as the reef.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and look, it is shaping up as a properly lovely spring stretch for the south east. We'll see plenty of blue sky through the weekend with daytime temps sitting in that comfortable low to mid twenties, so perfect jumper in the morning, tee shirt by lunch kind of weather. Brisbane and the Gold Coast can expect light winds and mostly dry conditions, though the Sunshine Coast hinterland might catch the odd stray shower overnight. And keep an eye on the sky Saturday night, because clear conditions mean south east Queenslanders should get a ripper view of that total lunar eclipse turning the moon a deep red. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Thanks Sam, and yeah, finals footy is exactly the kind of thing you want clear skies for. NRL finals are underway and AFL isn't far behind, with Queensland sides carrying plenty of hope into September. There's a real buzz around the state, pubs are already arguing about tipping and backyard barbecues are basically finals HQ for the next few weeks. Whatever happens, it's shaping up as a cracking finals series to watch. Nothing like September footy to bring people together, win lose or draw. Good luck to all our Queensland teams, we'll be cheering loud from the couch.

segments.script: So that's your Bright Side wrap for Friday, whales putting on a show, the reef getting a bit of help from science, and finals footy heating up right alongside spring sunshine. And don't forget to look up this weekend for that blood moon, it's the kind of free entertainment the universe doesn't offer very often. Genuinely one to step outside for. Big thanks to Jamie and to Sam for the weather, and to all of you for spending part of your day with us. It means a lot, truly. We'll be back same time next week with more good news from around Queensland and beyond. Until then, take care of each other. Get outside, look up at that moon, and we'll catch you on the next Bright Side. See ya.
